Subject: MAP: cost readiness scrub & eval checkpoints for Pulse Labs

Hi Sara / Pulse team —

Following our discovery, attaching an initial cost-readiness checklist and a lightweight eval plan so we can align MAP milestones against unit economics. Main asks: a short traffic profile, expected average prompt/response lengths, and which endpoints you plan to hit (chat vs. embeddings vs. reranking).

Quick background and what we want to validate in the MAP:
- Tokens/$ sanity: estimate tokens per user flow (prompt + avg response) and expected QPS. We’ll translate to tokens/day and estimated cost using current model profile.
- Caching assumptions: whether you can prefix-cache common prompts / system messages; opportunities for KV-cache reuse across sessions.
- Batching: target concurrency, acceptable latency SLOs (p50/p95), and whether micro-batching at the SDK side is possible.
- Eval plan: set of 20 representative prompts, 3 traffic buckets (low/medium/high), and a pilot QPS for the canary.

Deliverables we propose in the MAP (timeline below):
1) MAP workbook populated with your traffic numbers (see MAP-cost-scrub.xlsx).
2) Small eval run (eval-plan.yaml) to capture model token counts and latency under 3 batch sizes.
3) Joint canary (1 week) to exercise caching and steady-state batching.

Proposed high-level schedule:
- Dec 1: Kickoff + workbook share (this email)
- Dec 3: You return traffic/profile + sign off on test prompts
- Dec 6–10: Redwood runs eval permutations (batch sizes 1/4/8) and reports tokens/$ and latency matrix
- Dec 13–17: Canary pilot (joint)
- Dec 20: Review canary results and finalize SLA/close date proposal

Attachments: MAP-cost-scrub.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval-plan.yaml (yaml)

Thanks — if you want, Ben can run a short demo of batching/caching behavior with your sample prompts.

—
Olga Petrov

Thanks Olga — this looks good and very practical. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we fill the workbook: 

1) Token accounting: do you count both prompt + model output tokens against tokens/$? For our calculations we need to know if system messages and metadata are included.
2) Caching: our product has a lot of templated prompts (consent screens, triage prompts). Is prefix caching automatic or do we need to change how prompts are structured?
3) Pilot volume: for the canary we can commit to ~5k requests/day for the week if that helps with signal.

CC’ing procurement to make sure the MAP timelines are okay from their side. I’ll pull together a representative set of 20 prompts and a small synthetic traffic profile by Dec 3.

Sara — quick answers and a practical test matrix so you can populate the workbook with confidence.

Token accounting (short):
- Yes, tokens/$ counts both prompt + model output tokens. System messages and metadata that are sent as part of the request also count toward the prompt tokens.

Caching:
- Prefix caching is available but works best when you can split large system/context from per-user ephemeral content. If you can standardize a stable prefix (e.g., instructions + persona) we can cache the KV for that prefix and only re-send user-specific pieces.

Batching impact (empirical numbers we’ll run in the eval):
- Baseline (batch=1): p95 latency ~240ms, tokens/sec = 350
- batch=4: p95 latency ~320ms, tokens/sec = 1200 (better tokens/$)
- batch=8: p95 latency jumps ~520ms, tokens/sec = 2200 (useful for high-throughput async jobs)

Suggested eval matrix (what Redwood will run):
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8
- Traffic buckets: 100rps (high), 10rps (med), 1rps (low) — observe latency and tokens/sec
- Measures: tokens per request (prompt/output), p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k requests estimate

Operational asks we need from Pulse Labs:
- Representative prompt set (20 examples)
- Traffic profile (expected concurrency, peak QPS windows)
- Any latency SLOs (p50/p95) you must hit for user-facing flows

I’ll attach a lightweight script and example results after Redwood runs the permutations. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the sheet.

—
Ben Carter
